intro: Continents and oceans, natural disasters, and people who move from one country to another.
p.el inmigrante.nota: The feminine form is la inmigrante.
p.el emigrante.nota: The feminine form is la emigrante.
p.el extranjero.nota: As a person, la extranjera is the feminine form; en el extranjero means abroad.
p.el refugiado.nota: The feminine form is la refugiada; la persona refugiada is also common.
p.echar de menos.nota: Extrañar is also widely used, especially in Latin America.
b1.texto:
One common school model groups the world into **cinco continentes**; other models count them differently. There are several **océanos**: el Atlántico, el Pacífico, el Índico. Spain and Portugal share **la península** Ibérica.

Natural hazards include **un terremoto**, **un huracán**, **una inundación**, **una ola de calor**, **una ola de frío** and **granizo**. Spanish says **hubo** un terremoto, with **haber** in the indefinido.

People move. From the country they leave, they **emigran** and are **emigrantes**. From the country they reach, they **inmigran** and are **inmigrantes**. Someone who flees persecution or conflict may be **una persona refugiada** (also **un refugiado**).

Useful verbs: **irse a vivir a**, **cruzar** la frontera, **adaptarse a** otro país, **echar de menos** el suyo, **volver a** su país de origen.

Figures: **la población** de un país; **millones de** personas; **uno de cada diez**.
b2.f0: During the twentieth century, millions of Spaniards emigrated to the Americas and to northern Europe.
b2.f1: They left because there was no work in their country.
b2.f2: Today Spain receives immigrants from other continents, above all from the Americas and Africa.
b2.f3: Some cross the ocean by plane; others arrive by sea, on a very dangerous journey.
b2.f4: Adapting to another country is not easy: you have to learn the language and you miss your family.
b2.f5: Amal explains that, for now, she would not return to her country of origin if she could not have a safe life there.
b4.o0.refuerzo: Haber in the indefinido: there was.
b4.o1.refuerzo: Spanish says hubo for an event that took place.
b5.pregunta: Someone who arrives to live in your country is…
b5.o0.refuerzo: Seen from the country that receives him.
b5.o1.refuerzo: That is the view from the country he left.
b6.pregunta: According to the text, why did Spaniards emigrate?
b6.o0.refuerzo: En su país no había trabajo.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The text does not say that.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The text does not say that.
b7.o1: a hot wave in the sea
b7.o1.explicacion: Ola de calor is the set phrase for a heatwave.
b7.o2.explicacion: Ola is a wave. Hola is hello.
b8.pregunta: Complete: it is hard to adapt to another country.
b9.traduccion: Most would not go back to their country of origin.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about migration: why people leave their country, and the experience of someone you know.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Tell aloud what you would miss most if you had to live abroad, or what you do miss.
